defence.note: India defence production Rs1.78 tn in FY26; private sector 24% (Ministry of Defence via company presentation); Navy plans ~140 new ships (management, Aug-2026)

industry.tariffs: US tariffs and North American truck destocking cut standalone exports 15% in FY26 (Americas exports Rs3,317 cr to Rs2,487 cr). An India-US trade deal in early 2026 removed the punitive 25% duty (management, Feb-2026). US tariff on raw aluminium is 50% (Canadian supply), hurting BF's US aluminium plants.
industry.energyShock: The Iran war and LPG crisis (Q1FY27) raised energy and logistics costs (~160bp on standalone margin) and sent contract labour home (manpower 70-75% of normal in Aug-2026).

moat: Scale and process (forging)
Strong
India's largest forger; 0.2 kg to 30+ tonne parts; 7 forging and casting plants plus 21 machining/assembly sites in India; supplies most global truck OEMs for decades
A cost and capability lead in heavy, safety-critical parts that new entrants take years to qualify for
Customer qualification
Strong
Aerospace and large-engine parts take 3-5 years to approve; BF has supplied power-gen/data-centre engine parts for 15-18 years (Aug-2026 call)
Sticky business once won, but growth comes slowly
Defence platforms (KSSL)
Moderate
Indigenous artillery (ATAGS, co-developed with DRDO), CQB carbines, protected vehicles, naval turbines; Rs11,196 cr order book
Real capability, but government-paced: approvals slip, margins were 5-10% until FY26
Pricing power
Weak
Cost pass-through with a lag (Q1FY27 160bp hit); US tariffs absorbed (Rs12-31 cr a quarter in FY26)
A supplier to concentrated OEMs: it protects margins, it does not expand them
Overseas operations
Weak
EBITDA margin 1-4% for years; repeated restructuring; CDP to close
No advantage in Europe or US manufacturing; a drag on returns
Capital allocation
Mixed
JS Autocast a success (valued at ~3.5-4x cost by Premji Invest); e-mobility written off; two QIPs in two years
Good at Indian bolt-ons, poor overseas and in EVs
critiques: At ~94x trailing and ~41x our Sep-28E EPS the stock already prices defence and aerospace success; the DCF does not get close to the price.
Defence revenue was flat for three years (FY24-FY26 ~Rs1,420-1,570 cr) while the order book doubled: execution, not orders, is the issue.
Overseas operations have destroyed value for a decade (EBITDA ~1-4%, PBT losses of Rs330-470 cr a year); the CDP closure costs ~Rs358 cr and removes ~Rs1,600 cr of revenue.
GAM Research; Citi and Goldman questions on the Aug-2026 call
Two equity raises in two years (Rs1,650 cr in Dec-2024, Rs2,000 cr in Sep-2026) despite a "strong balance sheet": shareholders fund growth and M&A.
Exports depend on the North American truck cycle and US tariff policy (Americas exports -25% in FY26).
Bulls: defence order book 7x KSSL revenue, aerospace doubling, data-centre engines, CDP losses ending: EPS can double by FY28.
competition: Domestic forging peers are much smaller (Ramkrishna Forgings Rs4,238 cr FY26 revenue, Happy Forgings, CIE India); in defence BF competes with state firms (AWEIL, Munitions India) and private groups (Tata Advanced Systems, L&T, Adani Defence); globally with Thyssenkrupp, Sypris and Asian forgers.
